name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPR-410 Judge 'Bailiff'
description:
The Kang-Petrov KPR-410 is a five-shot revolver with an oversized cylinder chambered to accept both .410 bore shotshells and .45 Colt cartridges. The weapon features a three-inch rifled barrel and a frame that is noticeably wider than conventional revolvers to accommodate the shotshell cylinder. It is, in practical terms, a pocket shotgun that can also fire pistol ammunition.

The Bailiff's versatility is its selling point. Loaded with .410 shotshells, it fires a spread pattern effective for close-range defensive scenarios where precise aiming under stress is unreliable — the same logic that makes shotguns popular for home defense, miniaturized into a revolver. Loaded with .45 Colt, it functions as a conventional heavy-caliber revolver with better accuracy at range. The ability to mix ammunition types in the cylinder — shotshells for the first two chambers, .45 Colt for the remaining three — gives the shooter both close-range spread and medium-range precision in a single weapon.

Kang-Petrov markets the Bailiff as 'the district court' — a weapon that renders judgment at any range. The weapon has become popular among bouncers, building security, and transit operators who face threats at variable distances in confined spaces. Its distinctive wide cylinder makes it instantly recognizable, which provides a deterrence factor that its modest ballistic performance might not otherwise warrant.
legality: Legal — standard registration; shotshell capability noted on license
specifications: caliber: .410 bore / .45 Colt effective_range: 8 meters (.410), 30 meters (.45 Colt) rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver magazine_capacity: 5 rounds (cylinder) weight: 0.92 kg
tactical_use: A versatile close-range defensive revolver offering shotshell spread or pistol-caliber precision from a single weapon. The .410 shotshell provides a forgiving hit pattern for stress-fire situations at room distance. The .45 Colt round provides adequate stopping power at extended range. Ammunition can be mixed in the cylinder to provide both capabilities simultaneously.
cultural_context: The Bailiff is the bouncer's best friend — a weapon that doesn't require precision under the stress and chaos of a nightlife confrontation. Its wide cylinder and distinctive profile have made it an iconic weapon in the service industry security community. Carrying a Bailiff says 'I deal with problems up close and I don't always have time to aim.'
story_hooks: A Bailiff loaded with exotic .410 shells containing micro-flechettes is used in an attack — the flechettes are coated with a fast-acting paralytic agent, turning each shotshell into a non-lethal area-effect weapon.

A transit operator fires a .410 shotshell from their Bailiff in a crowded transit car and hits three people — the legal fallout questions whether shotshell-capable revolvers should be legal in enclosed public spaces.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stubbily aggressive revolver with a distinctly swollen, over-proportioned cylinder that dominates its silhouette. The barrel is short and businesslike, the frame chunky and utilitarian. It reads as compact but imposing — a pocket cannon masquerading as a sidearm.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 19 cm | Barrel length: 7.6 cm | Cylinder diameter: 4.2 cm (noticeably wider than standard revolvers) | Height: 13 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and dense. Feels substantial in the palm despite compact dimensions — the widened cylinder and reinforced frame concentrate mass in the user's hand, creating a grounded, purposeful heft.
physical_description.primary_material: Forged steel frame and cylinder with reinforced breech block. Polymer grip panels (thermoplastic composite rated for industrial use).
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on frame; the oversized cylinder sports a satin-brushed steel finish to showcase the dual-chamber architecture. Barrel and crane are deep charcoal with micro-stippling for corrosion resistance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed steel cylinder accents. Grip panels in charcoal-black polymer with subtle ribbing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Thermoplastic panels with pronounced crosshatch texture — designed for retention even with gloved or augmented hands. Edges beveled to prevent snagging.
distinctive_features: Visibly oversized cylinder with subtle longitudinal fluting to reduce weight while maintaining structural integrity
Wide forcing cone designed to accept .410 shotshell rims without binding
Kang-Petrov house mark stamped on the crane (a stylized angular 'K' interlocked with Cyrillic 'П')
Ammunition type markings etched into cylinder (small .410 symbol on chambers 1-2, .45 Colt markers on 3-5)
Custom loading gate with beveled edges for rapid reload under stress
Double-action trigger with subtle mechanical feedback ridge visible through the trigger guard
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS and KPR-410 JUDGE BAILIFF in serif font stamped on the left frame. Serial number engraved on the right-side crane. Caliber markings (.410/.45 LC) visible on the barrel rib. Tiny Cyrillic inspection marks on the frame underside.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and working. Light holster wear on the cylinder and frame corners. Occasional powder residue buildup visible in the chamber mouths. Grip panels may show minor scuffing from duty carry. This is a tool, not a collectible — honest wear is expected and accepted.
